issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a statutory provision on the ground that it violates the Constitution raises a question of constitutional interpretation.
material_facts: A statutory definition excluded certain debts, including debts due to a scheduled bank.
In a pending civil case before a subordinate court, the debtor challenged that exclusion as violating the constitutional guarantee of equal protection.
The debtor sought reference of the validity question and also asked the High Court to withdraw the case to decide the constitutional question.
issues.conclusion: The validity challenge also raised a question as to the interpretation of the Constitution and came within both the proviso to section 113 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Article 228 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 113 of the Code of Civil Procedure concerns the validity of an Act or a provision in an Act; Article 228 concerns a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution. A challenge to statutory validity based on an alleged contravention of a constitutional article raises a question of constitutional interpretation. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.pending_subordinate_case: A civil case was pending before a court subordinate to a High Court.
predicates.statutory_provision_challenged_under_con: A party in the pending case challenged a statutory provision as inconsistent with the Constitution.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge to a statutory provision arises in a pending case before a subordinate court, the challenge is a question of constitutional interpretation.

issues.legal_issue: The validity of a statutory provision must be decided before severability can be considered, even if the court considers that the provision would not be severable if invalid.
material_facts: The debtor pressed a constitutional challenge to the statutory exclusion because the outcome affected whether relief under the Act was available.
The lower courts considered the exclusion inseverable from the remainder of the definition and reasoned that the debtor would receive no relief in either event.
Whether the exclusion was severable could arise only if it was first held invalid.
issues.conclusion: It was necessary to decide the validity of the challenged portion to dispose of the case; the High Court was to withdraw the case and either dispose of it or determine the validity question and return it for disposal in accordance with that determination.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to section 113 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Article 228 of the Constitution, the relevant question must be necessary for disposal of the pending case. Severability is considered only after the challenged portion is held invalid, so a court cannot treat its view that the portion would be inseverable as a reason not to decide validity. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.pending_subordinate_case: A civil case was pending before a court subordinate to a High Court.
predicates.constitutional_validity_question_pressed: A party pressed a challenge to the validity of a statutory provision, and the answer affected the relief sought in the case.
predicates.severability_depends_on_invalidity: Whether the challenged part can be separated from the rest of the provision arises only if the challenged part is first held invalid.

issues.definition: If a pressed validity challenge affects the outcome of a pending subordinate-court case and severability depends on invalidity, validity must be decided before severability.
